0.content:
Alatyr (also: Alatyr Village): Alatyr is a remote village in Snezhnaya, abandoned several years before the Traveler arrives, and the hometown of the Rokot hunter Alyosha. A brutal winter bandit raid left its people destitute; when no help came, some villagers became highwaymen. The village cannot be visited in the game.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and inaccessible as of 7.1. It is only known through Alyosha's story and the Sretomorozsk episode of Chapter VII.

1.content:
Armory Palace (also: Royal Armory Palace): The Armory Palace, formally the Royal Armory Palace, is the Snezhnayan institution that develops weapons. Sandrone manages it, and it lies deep underground within Glupov, the Fatui's seat. It is closed to outsiders, guarded by Fatui troops and the Special Assignments Battalion, and is where the Landcruisers were engineered and where Project Mistilteinn's experiments take place.

History: The Armory Palace first appears in Version 6.0 (Luna I) content and is best known for developing the Landcruisers, automated war machines used by the Fatui across Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai.

Status as of 7.1: Active. As of 7.1 Project Mistilteinn is free to move forward after Ronova's fall, and the Armory Palace is investigating the application of life force.

2.content: Bratskaya (also: Bratskaya shop, Berezka): "Bratskaya" is a small general-goods shop in Zolnyy, the Ash District of Snezhnograd, in Snezhnaya. Its owner, Grigory, sells cooking ingredients and treats his regulars as neighbours rather than just customers.

3.content: Central Station (also: Snezhnograd Central Station, Central Railway Hub, Central Train Station): Central Station is the largest railway station in Snezhnaya, in the capital Snezhnograd. The official map text calls the railways the nation's veins and the Central Station the heart of a 'titan of cold iron and steel'. Arriving passengers pass inspections by Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau staff, then ride an elevator up to the heart of Snezhnograd.

4.content: Cloudborne Altar (also: Cloudborne Palace): The Cloudborne Altar is a summit ritual site above the clouds, high over the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak. Pavlina, the Snegurochka Grand Duchess, used it for the last stage of a rite meant to take the power of the Eye of Graeae. The Traveler reached it in the quest Bell Ringing at Dusk and stopped her there.

5.content: Court of Eternal Bliss (also: Court of Bliss, Courtyard of Carefree Light): The Court of Eternal Bliss, also called the Court of Bliss, is a chamber in the Pale Crown Palace where the Belyi Tsar's body lies sealed. Aksinya, the Tsar's former court jester, wanted to use it for a rite that would complete the Primordial Human and bring about a "Courtyard of Carefree Light". The Traveler stopped that rite here in the quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul.

6.content: Druzhna HQ (also: Druzhna Headquarters, Headquarters of the Druzhna): Druzhna HQ is the headquarters of the Druzhna in Snezhnograd, the capital of Snezhnaya. The Druzhna is the Tsaritsa's personal guard, led by Commander Vesna and made up mostly of Vila. The building is where the Tsaritsa's special recruitment drive to clear Shadow Realms is run by the officer Yarovaya.

7.content:
Everfrozen Earth (also: Everfrozen Earth region, Yongning Dongtu): Everfrozen Earth is the frozen northern region of Snezhnaya (first seen in 7.0). It holds the capital Snezhnograd, the Fatui headquarters city Glupov inside it, the fishing port of Morepesok and the Prime Ice mining station Svetloledovka. The ground is permanently frozen soil; the region is known for its birch forestry, a trade humanity carved out during Snezhnaya's pioneering era that still runs today.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is intact and open; nothing after 7.0 is recorded as changing it.

8.content:
Fellfrost Peak (also: Fellfrost Mountain): Fellfrost Peak is a giant snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd. On its summit stands the House of Hesperides, the mountain manor of the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess, said to own the whole mountain. A Prime Ice mining town lies at its foot and the fae Jack Frosts keep a hidden village on its slopes. Blizzards and a ban on unauthorised hiking keep visitors away.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mountain is open to explore, but its Grand Duchess Pavlina has died.

9.content:
Flamefeather Valley (also: Fiery Plumage Valley): Flamefeather Valley is a strange valley west of Snezhnograd that was once home to humans. Now almost nothing remains but a small town that turns up in ghost stories. It is named for the tall trees with leaves like flaming feathers, and for the bird-shaped monsters with crimson pinions that survivors report. Many curious explorers have gone in and never come back, though no official order forbids it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is quiet: Zhara and the Perfect Tree experiment are finished, and the village is empty.

10.content: Frozen Fulgurbranch: The Frozen Fulgurbranch is a bolt of lightning that froze solid mid-fall above the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak. It is a teleport waypoint on the way up to the Cloudborne Altar. The Snegovik Larisa's grief and fury, raised as a blizzard in her last hours, is said to have frozen it.

11.content: Frozen Royal Hall: The Frozen Royal Hall was the Belyi Tsar's throne room in the Pale Crown Palace. It still holds what the Eye of Graeae calls the very first Kresnik's Torch, a prototype that can be re-lit. The Traveler enters it in the quest The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated while looking for a fragment of the Eye's power.

12.content: Garden Bathed in Radiant Dew: The Garden Bathed in Radiant Dew is a garden at the House of Hesperides in Fellfrost Peak, kept alive amid the blizzard. It thrived under the care of Larisa, a Snegurochka who died during her own wedding, and its great tree has borne no fruit since. A fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power is hidden in that tree.

13.content:
Glupov (also: City of Fools, Fatui Headquarters): Glupov is a fortress-city in Snezhnaya, described as a satellite city within Snezhnograd, and the headquarters of the Fatui. Its name means "the city of fools". Its present Mayor is Pulcinella, "The Rooster", the Fifth of the Fatui Harbingers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Glupov remains the Fatui's headquarters under Mayor Pulcinella. No later change to its role is established.

14.content: Haeresys: Haeresys is an underground arena operated by the Fatui. It appears only in the official Genshin Impact manga, where captured test subjects are brought to fight unknown creatures as part of experiments.

15.content: Hall of Prayers (also: assembly hall, Grand Hall of Prayer, Koshchei's Hall): The Hall of Prayers, also called the assembly hall, is a ceremonial hall in the abandoned village of Okurov in Flamefeather Valley. The townspeople used to gather here and recite prayers that Doctor Moreau wrote for Zhara.

16.content:
House of Hesperides (also: Hesperides mansion, Hesperides manor, mountain manor of the Snegovik): The House of Hesperides is a remote mountain manor on Fellfrost Peak in Snezhnaya, the home of the Snegovik (snow fae) and their Grand Duchess. It was built thousands of years ago, and until Bell Ringing at Dusk it belonged to Pavlina, the Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka, who ruled its other residents.

History: According to the receptionist Raduzhnaya, the House of Hesperides was built thousands of years ago by the first Grand Duchess of the Snegovik, after the Belyi Tsar unified the north and set up the Pale Star Court.

17.content: Huntsman's Cabin (also: Hunter's Cabin, Workshop Beneath the Huntsman's Cabin): The Huntsman's Cabin is a cabin in the Volkodlak Tundra, Snezhnaya, where the hunter Alyosha's Meeting Point sits in a workshop beneath it. A fae gang once held it while guarding a prototype Kresnik's Torch and Shadow Realm antiques; after Alyosha and the Traveler clear it out, the torch warms a shelter for villagers who risk freezing.

18.content:
Hyperborea (also: Golden Hyperborea, Golden City, Hyperborean ruins): Hyperborea, called the Golden City, was a kingdom of Teyvat's ancient unified civilization, located where Snezhnaya lies today. Under the angel Koitar and the voyager Anacharsis it grew into a place of astonishing technology and then rose against the Heavenly Principles of Celestia. A Celestial Nail destroyed it, and its ruins sank into the Shadow Realm. Its survivors became the ancestors of the Frostmoon Scions of Nod-Krai.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hyperborea remains destroyed. No Hyperboreans live in the ruins and its history is held mainly by the Frostmoon Scions, the Belyi Tsar's notes and fragmentary item text.

19.content: Inverted Glacier: The Inverted Glacier is a Domain of Blessing in the Everfrozen Earth, the northern tundra of Snezhnaya. The domain text describes a barren mountain scourged by endless winter storms, where neither monsters nor outlaws can survive long in the ancient, desolate cold. Scoundrels who dwell there guard precious artifacts for anyone able to beat them.

20.content:
Jack Frost Village (also: Fae's Hidden Settlement): Jack Frost Village is the hidden homeland of the Jack Frosts, a small settlement on Fellfrost Peak in Snezhnaya. It was recently under siege by Volkodlaks until the Traveler helped the villagers fend them off, and it is the former home of the Geo Jack Frost Lumi, who now travels with Linnea.

Status as of 7.1: Inhabited by Jack Frosts as of 7.1. Its defences hold, and it has a shop open to adventurers.

21.content: Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop (also: Goodies Shop, Jack Frost goodies shop): The Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop is a trading post in Jack Frost Village where Jack Frosts swap goods they treat as "goodies" for uniquely crafted precision buttons. It is run by the Jack Frost Village Head.

22.content: The Korolevskiy Theater (also: Korolevskiy Theater, Korolevskiy Theatre, Royal Theater of Snezhnograd): The Korolevskiy Theater is the main theater of Snezhnograd, where the Korolevskiy Troupe stages ballet, opera and musical performances. It is favoured by the Fatui Harbingers and by Mitya, and it is the daily base of the prima ballerina Odette and the prima donna Vodyanitsa. Odette's Meeting Point is in the dressing room behind the stage.

23.content: Kresnik's Burning Heart (also: Ever-Burning Hearth Core, Central Kresnik's Torch chamber): Kresnik's Burning Heart is a large chamber under the central plaza of Snezhnograd, the capital of Snezhnaya. It holds the nation's most important Kresnik's Torch, a furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall ore to keep the city habitable. Staff of the Royal Energy Commission work there.

24.content: Kuznets (also: Kuznets smithy, Kuznets Workshop): "Kuznets" ("Blacksmith") is the smithy in Snezhnograd run by Kuzmichev, a domovoy blacksmith. It sits near the city's front gate.

25.content: Kvasnik (also: Kvasnik beverage shop): Kvasnik is a well-known beverage shop in Zolnyy, the Ash District of Snezhnograd, run by Zyryanov, a volkodlak. Its map description says the owner always claims that only his shop serves the most authentic kvass.

26.content: Lofty Clock Tower: The Lofty Clock Tower is a bell tower at the House of Hesperides, the Snegovik mountain manor in Fellfrost Peak. It stands on the manor's upper floors and holds large bells that can be rung. A guardian named Tsvetaev, an "Expedition Returner", defends it.

27.content:
Morepesok (also: Sea-Sand): Morepesok ("Sea-Sand") is a fishing settlement on the northern coast of Snezhnaya, in the Everfrozen Earth, and the hometown of Tartaglia (Childe), the Eleventh Fatui Harbinger. Boats go out from its harbor and a railway station links it to the rest of the country. Tartaglia's family, including his sister Tonia and youngest brother Teucer, lives here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Morepesok is a living fishing town. Tartaglia visits when his duties allow and, in the Travelers' Tales anecdotes added in 7.1, is shown buying gifts, planning to take Teucer ice fishing and promising Tonia to stay home longer next time.

28.content: Nastya's Home: Nastya's Home is a house in the abandoned village of Okurov where the young girl Nastya lived with her mother. "Nastya's Home" is an unofficial name for the place.

29.content:
Novokitezhgrad (also: New Kitezh, New Kitezhgrad, New Kitezh City): Novokitezhgrad ('New Kitezh') is a city in Snezhnaya southeast of Snezhnograd. It is famed for its liquor and its mining, above all of Kresnik Kristall, and many Snowland fae live there alongside humans. It was founded to replace Kitezhgrad, the old imperial capital destroyed by the Abyss. Players cannot visit it as of 7.1.

Status as of 7.1: Exists and works as a mining and liquor centre as of 7.1; never shown on screen.

30.content:
Okurov (also: Okurov Village): Okurov is an abandoned little town in Flamefeather Valley, Snezhnaya, with a warm climate and a dark history. Old stories say that nobody who goes in comes out. The whole area is played in third-person shooter mode.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Okurov stands abandoned. By the wiki's summary of the series, the experiments are exposed, the Eye of Graeae holds a crystal fragment of the ritual's power and Nastya has gone into the Perfect Tree.

31.content: Outdoor Hot Spring: The Outdoor Hot Spring is a facility in Everfrozen Earth built around a hot spring that appeared by accident. Humans and fae alike come here to enjoy a rare bit of warmth. It is kept up by an NPC named Kleyeva and is free for everyone.

32.content:
Pale Crown Palace (also: Palace of the Pale Crown, Belyi Tsar's mausoleum): The Pale Crown Palace is the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum in White Birch Snowgrave, Snezhnaya. Once one of his palaces, it became his tomb after he died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, and his body grew into the Tsar's White Birch, a pale mass of 'nerves' over the ruin. A hidden train line leads to it.

History: The Belyi Tsar welcomed humans and fae in this palace, and Kresnik's flame was first lit here. After he fell fighting the Abyss and its beasts during the Cataclysm, his remains were returned to the palace.

33.content:
Pilgrimage to the Sacred Gorge: The Pilgrimage to the Sacred Gorge is a snowy mountain gorge in the White Birch Snowgrave of Snezhnaya, on the way to the Pale Crown Palace, the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum. The route is blocked by a collapse that looks like an artificial avalanche, and official signs say the Royal Energy Commission and the Railway Transport Bureau are investigating.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the route to the Palace is still blocked and the investigation notice stands.

34.content:
Podvorye Restaurant (also: Podvorye, Ресторан «Подворье»): Podvorye Restaurant is a long-established eatery in front of Snezhnograd Square in Snezhnaya. It serves refined versions of traditional local dishes and Fire-Water, and its owner and entire staff are Volkodlak and other fae, who are long-lived. The owner, Nefedov, keeps it a dine-in house where food is served piping hot.

Status as of 7.1: Open and busy as of 7.1.

35.content:
Port Belovodye (also: Belovodye): Port Belovodye is a port in Snezhnaya that earns enormous sums. It is known chiefly from one historical episode: in the Tsaritsa's second year, its human inhabitants declared self-governance and rebelled against the fae princes, and in her third year the newly created Fatui brought them back, ending the revolt by negotiation.

Status as of 7.1: No events beyond the old revolt are shown; the port is not accessible in the game as of 7.1.

36.content:
Rankova Zorya: Rankova Zorya is a railway halt in the Volkodlak Tundra of Snezhnaya that was nearly abandoned until Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa, with the Traveler's help, renovated it. It now has a furnace, a stage, a Bing-Bang Finchball stall and a restaurant, and new residents have arrived. In 7.1 the battle against Ronova, the Ruler of Death, took place here.

Status as of 7.1: A living village as of 7.1. Its founders are busy with other work, so they visit instead of living there permanently.

37.content: Relics of the Fallen Grace: Relics of the Fallen Grace is a Domain of Mastery on Fellfrost Peak, the great snow-sloped mountain south of Snezhnograd. According to its text it is a sanctuary once built by the ancient fae and now despoiled by petty brigands. Clearing it grants talent materials, described in game as insight and enlightenment.

38.content: Restaurant Zorya (also: Rankova Kafe, Zorya Restaurant): Restaurant Zorya is a re-opened restaurant in Rankova Zorya, in the Volkodlak Tundra. Tolstaya runs it and sells food and recipes there.

39.content:
The Ruined Hvergelmir (also: Ruined Hvergelmir, Hvergelmir research institute, Hvergelmir ruins): The Ruined Hvergelmir is what remains of the Hvergelmir research institute in Snezhnaya's White Birch Snowgrave, below the Belyi Tsar's Pale Crown Palace. It was a secret bio-alchemy and Shadow Realm institute founded by the Belyi Tsar and entrusted to his human ward Aksinya, with a goal of engineering a "Proto-Man" who would let the Tsar become the Primordial Human. It holds four laboratories belonging to Aksinya, Alvis, Koshchei and Pavlina.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the institute is a ruin. Aksinya remains trapped in the Shadow Realm after her defeat.

40.content: Sadov-Arbat (also: Garden Arbat): Sadov-Arbat is a long-established handicrafts and souvenir shop in Snezhnograd. According to its map description, in the Belyi Tsar's time the site was a market where fae bartered with one another before it became a proper shop.

41.content:
Sanctuary of Grief (also: Signora's tomb): The Sanctuary of Grief is the tomb of Signora, the Eighth Fatui Harbinger, in the Everfrozen Earth of Snezhnaya. It is an ice-sealed palace built after she died in Inazuma, where she lost to the Traveler and was executed. The remaining Harbingers arranged her burial here, and Fatui work was halted for half a day to mourn her. The mood is cold, quiet mourning.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sanctuary stands intact as Signora's tomb in the Everfrozen Earth.

42.content: Scars of Cursed Obsession: Scars of Cursed Obsession is a Forgery domain in Snezhnaya's Everfrozen Earth. Its description calls it a secret haven where rebels chased the dream of a return to the old order, a dream that died in crimson fire and left only ash. Clearing it grants weapon ascension materials.

43.content:
Snezhnaya (also: Snezhnayan, Land of Snow, Nation of Eternal Winter): Snezhnaya is the Cryo nation of perpetual winter in the far north of Teyvat. It worships the Tsaritsa (Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya), Cryo Archon and God of Love, who unlike most Archons rules directly and absolutely from Zapolyarny Palace in the capital, Snezhnograd. Her Fatui act as government, diplomats and army, and her goal is to overthrow the Heavenly Principles. Humans share the land with the Snowland Fae, the old aristocracy of her predecessor the Belyi Tsar, and survive the cold by burning Kresnik Kristall in great furnaces called Kresnik's Torches.

History: Long ago the land was green and held golden Hyperborea, destroyed about 6,000 years ago. The Belyi Tsar united the fae and became the first Cryo Archon 2,000 years ago; he died fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, and Anastasya succeeded him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Snezhnaya has defeated the Shade of Death, Ronova, whose curse killed anyone developing anti-Celestia technology. The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, Project Mistilteinn has resumed, and the Traveler serves her as a consultant.

44.content:
Snezhnograd (also: Snow City, Snezhnograd City, Capital of Snezhnaya): Snezhnograd, "Snow City", is the capital of Snezhnaya, a blizzard-country city kept habitable by Kresnik's Torch. It holds the Tsaritsa's Zapolyarny Palace, the Snezhnograd Veche, the Druzhna headquarters and the Adventurers' Guild's headquarters. Pulcinella, "The Rooster", is its Mayor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Snezhnograd is the working capital of Snezhnaya under the Tsaritsa and Mayor Pulcinella, with its Torch burning and alchemy still outlawed.

45.content: Snezhnograd Veche State Hall (also: Veche State Hall, Snezhnograd Veche meeting hall): The Snezhnograd Veche State Hall is where the Snezhnograd Veche, Snezhnaya's legislative assembly, holds its regular meetings. Citizen representatives from different groups discuss newly issued laws there, a tradition kept since the early days of the nation. It is presided over by 'The Rooster', the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella.

46.content: Snowmelt Drainage Channel: The Snowmelt Drainage Channel is an underground system beneath Okurov, the strange town in Flamefeather Valley. It was meant to carry snowmelt away so the valley basin would not flood. According to the wiki it was built on the orders of Koshchei, who also used it as a laboratory.

47.content:
Sretomorozsk (also: Candlemas-Frost City, Sretomorozsk Station): Sretomorozsk is a quiet border town in the southwest of Snezhnaya, a railway station and port that connects the country with Nod-Krai. In Chapter VII it is where the Traveler first sees the effects of Project Stuzha: homes are cold, inns are closed and the station is shut. Alyosha, who keeps a small place there, uncovers a Kristall-hoarding scheme.

Status as of 7.1: By 7.1 the corruption has been exposed, the Fatui supervise distribution and have promised that the station will resume service, but the shortages are not over: Alyosha notes Project Stuzha is not going away soon. Sretomorozsk continues to serve as the transit town for Nod-Krai traffic.

48.content:
Svetloledovka (also: Light-Ice Village, Prime Ice Excavation Site): Svetloledovka ('Light-Ice Village') is a Prime Ice mining town and railway station in Snezhnaya, built in the shadow of Fellfrost Peak. Many of its workers live in Snezhnograd and commute by train. In Chapter VII a malfunction and a monster trapped miners here, and the Traveler first met Odette during the rescue.

Status as of 7.1: Inhabited and functioning as of 7.1, with the monster's cave closed and the machines reinforced. Sandrone expected relief to take weeks to months.

49.content: Tartaglia's Home (also: Ajax's family home, Tartaglia family home): Tartaglia's Home is the home of Tartaglia's family in Morepesok, a small seaside fishing village in Snezhnaya. Tartaglia, called Ajax at home, grew up here, and his younger sister Tonia and little brother Teucer live there. He seldom visits, which is the main thing the people at the house talk about.

50.content:
Teeming Mire (also: Tree Swamp Where Lifeforms Live): The Teeming Mire is the sunken, tree-choked heart of Okurov, the hidden town in Snezhnaya's Flamefeather Valley. Below the assembly hall a giant tree grows among blue algae: the home of the so-called Perfect Tree, an experiment by the bio-alchemist Koshchei, who posed as Doctor Moreau. It is guarded by the firebird Zhara, and it is where the child Nastya chose to be transformed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Mire holds the Perfect Tree with Nastya now blue algae, and the ritual's power has been returned to the Eye of Graeae.

51.content:
Tidesong Cavern (also: Cavern of Melodic Tides): Tidesong Cavern is a hidden cave on Fellfrost Peak, the snowy mountain south of Snezhnograd in Snezhnaya, and the private practice space of the Water Imp Vodyanitsa. A flooded cave with a giant shell and a few Prime Ice echo pillars, it gives her voice the acoustics she wants and keeps her audience away.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern is Vodyanitsa's working private retreat, with its pillars repaired and the Meeting Point available.

52.content: Torchlight Books (also: Enlightened Torch): Torchlight Books is a bookshop in Snezhnograd owned by Moes. It stocks books on Snezhnayan history and ballet.

53.content: Train (also: Your Train, the Traveler's train): The Train is the Traveler's personal base in Snezhnaya: a large train summoned by the Eye of Graeae and made to run on the iron rails crossing the frozen tundra. It lets the Traveler reach the region's stations and carries a shooting range, crafting bench and firearm loadout display.

54.content: Train Boneyard: The Train Boneyard is a point of interest in Everfrozen Earth, a graveyard of old trains. In the world quest Disputes Without Honor and Humanity it is where Vasiliy, the Izmaylov family's "Young Sire", made his last stand. Zmei and Sofya say "train boneyard" is just a nickname used by locals.

55.content:
VIP Lounge (also: Lounge for Honored Guests, House of Hesperides VIP room): The VIP Lounge is a room on the second floor of the House of Hesperides, the mountain manor of the Snegovik in Fellfrost Peak, Snezhnaya, set aside for honoured guests. A guard at the door admits only holders of a VIP Pass, a gilded letter said to be issued by the manor's mistress. Inside, a main hall and a side room hold tables for guests who come to drink and rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lounge is accessible to anyone who finds a pass.

56.content:
Volkodlak Tundra (also: Tundra of Ancient Beasts): The Volkodlak Tundra is called the "Tundra of Ancient Beasts". It is said to have been the site of the capital of the Miscislavli Alliance, a confederation ruled by the great Volkodlak lord Miscislav. When the Belyi Tsar's spear pierced Miscislav's head and his horsemen scattered the alliance, everything here was demolished and rebuilt, with no trace left of the old city. The Archon Quest of Snezhnaya begins in the tundra, at the village of Rankova Zorya.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing beyond the revival of Rankova Zorya is recorded here.

57.content:
White Birch Snowgrave (also: Snow-Entombed Crownlands): White Birch Snowgrave was the itinerant court of the Belyi Tsar and became his mausoleum after he died in the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. Its palace, the Pale Crown Palace, is both palace and ruin: once the seat from which the ancient Tsars ruled, now their final resting place. From it sprang the giant Tsar's White Birch, a sign that the Tsar still watches over Snezhnaya.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grave is quiet, with the Tsar's White Birch still standing.

58.content:
Zapolyarny Palace (also: Palace Beyond the Arctic Circle, Glacial Palace of the Polestar, Tsaritsa's palace): Zapolyarny Palace stands in Snezhnograd, Snezhnaya's capital, and is the residence from which the Cryo Archon rules. The Belyi Tsar held court here until his death in the cataclysm 500 years ago; Tsaritsa Anastasya has reigned from it since. It looks wrought from ice and snow, everything inside revolves around the Tsaritsa, and it holds her throne room (where she holds court with Harbingers and ministers), her private office and, in a hidden basement, a seal left by the Third Descender.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the palace remains Anastasya's seat of rule. The Traveler may come and go freely and acts as her informal consultant. The Third Descender's seal beneath it is still closed; Anastasya holds six Gnoses, and the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

59.content:
Zolnyy (also: Ash District, Zolnyy District): Zolnyy is the industrial "Ash District" of Snezhnograd, the capital of Snezhnaya. Its official map description says that even amid ashes a person may hold fast to a dream, perhaps how the district got its name. It holds ordinary residents, a kvass shop, a general store and the stronghold of the Luchkin, one of the fae gangs of the High Table.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Zolnyy is peaceful. The Luchkin remain under Zmei, and the Izmaylov gang lacks a leader.
